source_contract: u/v dimensions time,siglay,nele: velocity stored at triangle faces; temp stored at nodes.

official_face_centres_check.interpretation: Arithmetic triangle centroids match official lonc/latc within about3m; no face ordering or component rotation mismatch.

diagnosis.source_integrity: Source triangle order and east/north interpretation are correct; selected23snapshot mean reproduces within rounding.
diagnosis.underlying_feature: A broad low-speed mean shear/reversal band exists in source model values.
diagnosis.display_artifact: Piecewise constant face vectors introduce abrupt mesh-aligned jumps. At some adjacent triangles the two vectors point away from their shared edge, creating particle depletion exactly on that geometric edge. Display minimum boost amplifies initial separation. Sharp repeated sawtooth is a mesh reconstruction artifact, not reliable physical shape.
diagnosis.proposed_fix: Reconstruct a continuous bounded display vector field within existing wet triangles. Preserve original face-centre values using shared reconstructed mesh-node values and three face-centre subtriangles per source triangle. Use nonnegative weights and barycentric interpolation; do not modify source averages or extend across wet-mask edges.

recommended_reconstruction_checks: Every original valid face centre reproduces its original east/north vector to floating point tolerance.
Across a shared edge, both face-side reconstructions approach the identical shared-edge value; no discrete jump remains.
Nonnegative nodal/point weights keep each component within the convex hull of local valid samples; original data arrays stay unchanged.
Retain the original wet-triangle mask and null faces. Do not interpolate across islands, masked holes, separate vertex fans or beyond source extent.
Shared node reconstruction should use an edge-connected incident-face fan if separate fluid regions meet only at a vertex.
Do not claim conservation, local current validation or removal of the actual broad mean shear/stagnation; this is display reconstruction.
Retest actual trajectories and encoded trail ink in the band: a smoother background alone does not prove the depletion seam is resolved.
